A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Encryption-Friendly LLM Architecture. Their complete main texts, Appendices A–H, equations, tables, and figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original encrypted fine-tuning and inference timings, GLUE results, and supplementary computational and precision analyses, including Tables 2–4 and 15–16.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and reports revised matrix-multiplication timings in Table 1a.

M1.justification: The LoRA/Gaussian-kernel transformer, AdamW-HE optimizer, penalty training, and optimized packing and matrix-multiplication procedures remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–5 and the appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CoLA, MRPC, RTE, STS-B, SST-2, and QNLI under the same encrypted fine-tuning and inference scenarios. No dataset, task, domain, or evaluated scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 4 retain their full-fine-tuning/LoRA and softmax/GK comparison variants. The HETAL-based softmax and Rectangular MM comparisons also remain. Newly cited P3EFT and Skyformer are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The two-layer configuration, LoRA rank 2, 128-token timings, training budgets, metrics, and appendix hyperparameters remain unchanged. Table 1a retains the stated 128×768 by 768×768 matrix sizes despite its revised timing values.

E4.justification: The optimization, dimension-scaling, polynomial-approximation, and HE/plaintext agreement analyses retain the same tables and figures in Appendices D–H. Appendix G updates its quotation of the Table 1 ratio without adding or redesigning an analysis.

E5.justification: Section 5.3 still reports ten repetitions per plaintext task and selection of the best score. Seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged; no confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 1a changes CCMM from 1.095 to 1.259 seconds and PCMM from 0.103 to 0.275 seconds, revising their ratio from 10.63× to 4.58×. Section 5.2 and Appendix G follow this revision, which agrees with Table 15a already present in v1. End-to-end timings and GLUE scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 newly specifies a semi-honest adversary that follows the protocol while collecting outputs, and explicitly grounds security in CKKS semantic security. This adds an explicit security assumption; the mathematical definitions, derivations, and operation-count analyses otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same architecture and privacy-preserving fine-tuning/inference claims, including 6.94× fine-tuning and approximately 2.3× inference speedups with performance comparable to plaintext models.

C2.justification: The new semi-honest-model paragraph makes the security guarantee's applicability to protocol-following adversaries explicit. The existing exclusion of model-weight stealing and the computational limitations remain, so this is a limited but substantive clarification of security scope.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and GitHub repository link in the abstract and footnote 1, absent from v1. Hardware, hyperparameters, packing algorithms, and polynomial-approximation details are otherwise unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds P3EFT (Li et al., 2024), distinguishing its emphasis on energy consumption. Section 4 adds Skyformer (Chen et al., 2021) to the Gaussian-kernel and low-rank-attention antecedents. These are limited additions to the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds short security and related-work passages, a code note, and acknowledgements, and reverses the two co-senior authors' order. The main narrative, section sequence, and Appendix A–H organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds ICLR 2025 running headers and introduces small spacing, line-wrapping, and page-break changes. Figures 1–9, table structures, and algorithm displays are retained without substantive redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 resolves the Table 1a/Table 15a timing inconsistency, explicitly states the semi-honest security boundary, and adds relevant prior-work attribution and a code-access pointer. These provide limited gains in consistency, scope clarity, and reproducibility documentation while the method, principal experimental findings, and evaluation breadth remain unchanged.
